WOODWORK — MOCK EXAM #11
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: WOODWORK
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When learning Furniture Making, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Furniture Making.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Furniture Making.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Furniture Making.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Furniture Making.

2. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Overload every socket
   B. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun
   C. Never touch live wires with wet hands
   D. Ignore burnt cables

3. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Run with the tool
   B. Wear safety gear and follow instructions
   C. Work alone with eyes closed
   D. Remove all guards

4. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. Speaker
   B. Keyboard
   C. CPU
   D. Monitor

5. When learning Entrepreneurship in Woodwork, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Entrepreneurship in Woodwork.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Entrepreneurship in Woodwork.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Entrepreneurship in Woodwork.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Entrepreneurship in Woodwork.

6. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. International Cricket Team
   B. Input Cable Tester
   C. Internal Cooking Timer
   D. Information and Communication Technology

7. When learning Occupational Information, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Occupational Information.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Occupational Information.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Occupational Information.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Occupational Information.

8. When learning Emergency Management, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Emergency Management.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Emergency Management.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Emergency Management.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Emergency Management.

9. When learning Upholstery, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Upholstery.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Upholstery.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Upholstery.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Upholstery.

10. When learning Project Activity, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Project Activity.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Project Activity.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Project Activity.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Project Activity.

11. When learning Blending wood with other materials, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Blending wood with other materials.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Blending wood with other materials.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Blending wood with other materials.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Blending wood with other materials.

12. When learning Design in Woodwork, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Design in Woodwork.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Design in Woodwork.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Design in Woodwork.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Design in Woodwork.

13. When learning Fittings, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Fittings.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Fittings.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Fittings.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Fittings.

14. When learning Framed Wooden Doors and Windows, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Framed Wooden Doors and Windows.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Framed Wooden Doors and Windows.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Framed Wooden Doors and Windows.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Framed Wooden Doors and Windows.

15. When learning Estimation of Materials, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Estimation of Materials.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Estimation of Materials.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Estimation of Materials.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Estimation of Materials.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Blending wood with other materials and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
